identity: Visual artist and film director · United States · 1928–1987
title: Andy Warhol's birth chart
metaDescription: Andy Warhol's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 13.9° Leo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Leo — the Sun, Mercury, Venus and Neptune. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 13.9° Leo, inside the second decan (10°–20°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Jupiter. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 3.6° Leo, Venus was at 23.9° Leo, Mars was at 28.4° Taurus. Read together: thought that arrives already in motion; attraction declared rather than implied; effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Mars square Neptune, 0.0° of separation. Nothing in a square flows; everything in it works. The old texts kept squares for the charts they respected. Behind it, the Sun trine Saturn at 1.3°, and Mercury trine Uranus at 3.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: the Sun, Saturn, Uranus close a triangle of trines. A grand trine is read as self-sufficiency in one element: the current circulates whether or not anything is asked of it.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, two placements stand out. The Sun in Leo at 13.9° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mars in Taurus at 28.4° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 7 fire, 2 earth, 1 water by element and 6 fixed, 3 cardinal, 1 mutable by modality. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Saturn and Uranus were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Aries for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.9° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 17.0°.
